title: Electrical Wiring Safety
summary: Electrical hazards are a leading cause of construction deaths. Wiring a circuit that is still live causes shock, burns, and falls. This talk covers de-energizing, verifying, and insulated tools.
talking_points: De-energize circuits before doing any work on them.
Use lockout devices so the circuit cannot go live, and tag the locked device so no one turns it on.
Clearly identify which power source and circuits are disconnected.
Use an AC voltage tester to verify the power is actually off before you touch conductors.
Use insulated tools and insulated gloves when working on wires.
site_hazards_to_check: Panel or circuit not locked and tagged before wiring work
No voltage tester used to confirm the circuit is dead
Uninsulated or damaged hand tools used on or near conductors
Wet conditions around the wiring work area
Unlabeled disconnects, so it is unclear which circuits are off
discussion_questions: What steps do you take before stripping or landing a wire?
How do you know the tester itself is working before you trust it?
Which tools in your bag are rated and insulated for live-adjacent work?

flags: OSHA mapping verified accurate: 1926.416 (general requirements, incl. insulated tools/PPE at 416(a)) and 1926.417 (lockout and tagging of circuits). De-energize, lock/tag, identify the source, verify with an AC tester, use insulated tools and gloves - all consistent with the standard. No tolerance issues.
